reply.rationale: No defensible compositional paradigm survives the evidence requirements. A few surface similarities are tempting (e.g. HU/HL, the candidate Cor/ll/ft families, and pairs like HighI/HI or AlignColl/AC), but they do not yield a supported network of substitution classes and constructions whose parts make stable, reusable contributions across multiple entries. HU/HL does show a possible contrast in a shared frame, but analyzing it would require a root slot with only H and no demonstrated substitutional paradigm; the rest of the codebook does not provide matching forms like CU/CL or NU/NL. The suggested Cor/ll/ft splits fail semantic compositionality: the residues do not form coherent shared frames with predictable meanings. Abbreviation-like pairs such as AlignColl~AC and HighI~HI are whole-code aliases, not concatenative morphology. Therefore the safest complete analysis is a flat lexicon.
